milestones.title: P1Y — Assistant Replacement & Provider Parity
milestones.description: Make Laravel AI Agent Kit a credible functional replacement for Laravel AI Assistant by closing missing capability gaps, hardening provider parity, preserving package-owned orchestration semantics, and adding migration ergonomics only where they are truly required.

issues.title: P1Y-I1 Define assistant replacement surface + compatibility contract
issues.summary:
Define the package-owned assistant-replacement target by auditing the real feature surface relied on by `laravel-ai-assistant` users and translating that audit into an explicit capability-coverage target for Laravel AI Agent Kit.

This issue is not docs-first migration work. It is the scoping issue that determines which user-facing capabilities are already covered by current agent-kit SSOT, which are partially covered, which are missing, and which are intentionally out of scope.
issues.rationale:
The package already has orchestrator, blueprint, provider-profile, tool-governance, memory, and telemetry foundations. What is still missing is a precise, implementation-driving statement of which assistant-era capabilities matter and what must be present so switching users do not lose meaningful functionality.

Without this audit and target definition, later work risks optimizing for API mimicry, documentation, or speculative parity instead of the real missing capability delta.
scope: Audit the practical feature surface of `laravel-ai-assistant` that users depend on, grounded in its actual repository SSOT
Classify each capability as covered, partially covered, missing, or intentionally out of scope in current `laravel-ai-agent-kit` SSOT
Define the package-owned replacement target in capability terms rather than one-to-one API terms
Identify the real blockers that would cause switching users to lose meaningful functionality
Translate the audit into concrete downstream implementation targets for provider parity, structured output, staged workflows, memory, tools, and ergonomics
out_of_scope: Implementing the missing capability gaps
Adding a migration facade or compatibility wrapper before the audit proves it is needed
Writing a migration guide before capability closure is understood
Marketing or release announcement language
dependencies: P1X-I3 Implement orchestrator core + execution tree + final orchestration result
P1X-I9 `TextToStructuredEvaluation` blueprint over orchestrator
P1X-I11 `AudioToTextToEvaluation` blueprint over orchestrator
acceptance_criteria: An explicit capability matrix exists for assistant-era user expectations, classified as covered, partially covered, missing, or intentionally out of scope.
The matrix is grounded in the latest SSOT for both packages and does not rely on guesswork or API-name matching alone.
The replacement target is defined in package-owned capability terms, not raw provider or legacy API terms.
The audit identifies the concrete missing delta that later issues must implement so switching users do not lose meaningful functionality.
The resulting target is usable as the scoping reference for all remaining P1Y issues.
tests: Analysis/spec issue; add contract tests only if new package-owned capability DTOs or interfaces are introduced as part of the scoping output
Static/architecture checks only if new public contract surfaces are introduced
risks: Risk of auditing too shallowly and missing real assistant-era user workflows
Risk of auditing too broadly and creating an unbounded parity backlog
Risk of drifting toward API mimicry instead of package-owned capability coverage
docs: Capture the capability matrix in package docs or planning docs only after the audit is complete
Reference the audited capability matrix from later parity and readiness issues

issues.title: P1Y-I2 Implement assistant-style facade / adapter over orchestrator
issues.summary:
Implement a package-owned assistant-style facade or adapter over orchestrator-backed execution only if the P1Y-I1 audit proves that a dedicated migration-oriented entrypoint is necessary for meaningful developer ergonomics.

This issue exists to cover real migration friction, not to force a one-to-one assistant API clone.
issues.rationale:
Users switching from `laravel-ai-assistant` may need a simpler package-owned entrypoint for common assistant-style use cases. However, that should only be added if the audit proves existing blueprints and orchestrator surfaces are not sufficient to preserve meaningful functionality without unnecessary friction.

A compatibility-oriented facade can be valuable, but only if it closes a real capability or ergonomics gap without undermining the package’s architecture.
scope: Use the P1Y-I1 audit to determine whether a dedicated assistant-style package entrypoint is actually required
If required, implement a package-owned facade or adapter that resolves into orchestrator- or blueprint-backed execution internally
Keep request/result DTOs package-owned and free of provider SDK types
Preserve package memory semantics, provider-profile routing, tool governance, telemetry, and typed package failures
Avoid introducing a second unconstrained public API that bypasses existing package architecture
out_of_scope: One-to-one cloning of `laravel-ai-assistant` APIs
Exposing provider-native assistant, thread, run, or message objects
Bypassing orchestrator, blueprints, provider policy, or package memory semantics
Weakening tool-governance or telemetry defaults
dependencies: P1Y-I1 Define assistant replacement surface + compatibility contract
acceptance_criteria: The need for a dedicated assistant-style entrypoint is explicitly justified by the audited capability matrix from P1Y-I1.
If implemented, the facade or adapter remains package-owned and orchestration-backed.
If the audit shows no dedicated compatibility entrypoint is necessary, this issue can be resolved by an explicit no-op decision and documented rationale.
No provider SDK types leak into the facade, adapter, or any new public package DTOs.
Existing package security, memory, telemetry, and provider-profile rules remain intact.
tests: Unit tests for any new package-owned adapter request/result DTOs
Integration tests proving the facade delegates to orchestrator- or blueprint-backed execution deterministically
Architecture/static checks for no vendor-type leakage if a new public compatibility surface is introduced
risks: Risk of introducing a misleading assistant-clone surface that drifts from package architecture
Risk of adding an unnecessary facade when existing package workflows are already sufficient
Risk of migration confusion if ergonomics work is attempted before capability gaps are closed
docs: Document the facade only if it is actually implemented
If not implemented, record the rationale that existing package surfaces are the preferred migration path
issues.execution_note: Do not start this issue until P1Y-I1 is complete. This is a conditional ergonomics issue, not a mandatory compatibility-clone issue.

issues.title: P1Y-I3 Structured output normalization + repair pipeline
issues.summary:
Harden package-owned structured-output execution so switching users receive stable package-shaped structured results even when provider output formatting, refusal behavior, or JSON fidelity differs.

The goal is capability coverage, not provider passthrough.
issues.rationale:
Structured output is one of the most important places where users will feel feature loss when moving from a simpler assistant package into agent-kit. Current package blueprints already depend on package-owned structured result shapes, but cross-provider reliability and malformed-output handling remain a real parity risk.

If this is not hardened, users may technically have a feature on paper while still losing reliable behavior in practice.
scope: Introduce a package-owned normalization layer for structured-output execution paths
Differentiate valid structured output, repairable malformed output, refusal-style output, and unrecoverable output
Preserve package-owned output DTOs and validation rules
Return typed package failures instead of leaking raw provider-specific malformed responses
Keep the normalization logic provider-neutral at the public boundary
out_of_scope: Adding arbitrary caller-defined output schema systems
Exposing raw provider JSON as the stable package contract
Provider-specific public DTOs or error payloads
dependencies: P1Y-I1 Define assistant replacement surface + compatibility contract
P1X-I9 `TextToStructuredEvaluation` blueprint over orchestrator
acceptance_criteria: Package-owned structured-output flows can distinguish valid, repairable, refusal, and unrecoverable outputs deterministically.
Structured-output results remain package-owned and stable across providers.
Malformed provider output does not leak through the public package boundary as raw payloads.
Typed package failures exist for the main structured-output failure classes.
The implementation is reusable across the relevant blueprint and orchestrator-backed structured-output paths.
tests: Unit tests for normalization and repair decision paths
Integration tests for structured-output blueprint flows using deterministic fake runtime responses
Negative-path tests for malformed JSON, refusal payloads, and unrecoverable output
risks: Risk of overfitting normalization to one provider’s malformed-output patterns
Risk of accidental contract drift in package-owned structured result DTOs
Risk of silent repair masking real failures if failure classes are under-specified
docs: Document package-owned structured-output guarantees once the runtime behavior is hardened

issues.title: P1Y-I4 Provider capability matrix + conformance suite
issues.summary: Create a provider capability matrix and deterministic conformance suite that proves which provider profiles can actually satisfy the assistant-era capabilities users care about when switching to agent-kit.
issues.rationale:
Provider neutrality is only useful if the package can prove capability coverage in practice. The package already has provider-profile and capability concepts, but the missing step is a conformance layer grounded in the audited replacement target rather than optimistic profile declarations alone.

This issue converts the audited capability target into an executable, regression-proof provider matrix.
scope: Define the provider capability matrix for the audited replacement target from P1Y-I1
Cover the relevant package capabilities such as text generation, structured output, audio transcription, tool-capable execution, memory-aware continuation, and staged workflows where applicable
Add deterministic conformance tests for declared provider-profile capabilities
Fail explicitly when a configured profile claims a capability the package cannot actually rely on
Keep the capability model package-owned and free of provider-specific public contract leakage
out_of_scope: Adding new provider SDK integrations outside the existing runtime substrate
Publishing marketing compatibility claims without deterministic package tests
Treating provider declarations as sufficient without behavior-level proof
dependencies: P1Y-I1 Define assistant replacement surface + compatibility contract
P1-I2 Provider profiles + selection policy over Laravel AI SDK
P1X-I5 Implement provider profile assignment + capability compatibility for agents
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic provider capability matrix exists for the audited assistant-era capability target.
The package can prove which configured provider profiles satisfy which relevant capabilities.
Capability mismatches fail explicitly and are regression-covered.
The conformance suite is package-owned and does not leak provider SDK types into public contracts.
Later parity and readiness issues can rely on the matrix as their test foundation.
tests: Unit tests for capability matching and mismatch behavior
Integration tests for provider-profile conformance using deterministic fake runtime behavior
Negative-path tests for false capability claims and unsupported staged combinations
risks: Risk of under-specifying capability semantics and producing false confidence
Risk of provider profile declarations drifting away from real behavior
Risk of coupling the matrix too tightly to one provider’s execution quirks
docs: Document the provider capability matrix once it is backed by tests and stable package behavior

issues.title: P1Y-I5 Tests: cross-provider `TextToStructuredEvaluation` parity
issues.summary: Add deterministic cross-provider parity coverage for `TextToStructuredEvaluation` so the package can prove the flagship structured-evaluation workflow preserves the same package-owned result semantics across supported provider profiles.
issues.rationale:
This blueprint is one of the clearest migration-facing package surfaces. If switching users see different behavior, missing dimensions, broken structure, or provider-shaped failures here, they will experience that as lost functionality even if the package is technically more advanced.

This issue turns the flagship text blueprint into a parity reference workflow.
scope: Exercise `TextToStructuredEvaluation` against the provider profiles validated by the P1Y-I4 capability matrix
Assert stable package-owned result DTO shape across providers
Assert provider-profile routing and fallback behavior where applicable
Assert structured-output normalization behavior from P1Y-I3 within the flagship workflow
Keep the tests fully deterministic with package or SDK fakes
out_of_scope: Live provider execution
Benchmark or performance testing
Adding new public result-shape variants for different providers
dependencies: P1Y-I3 Structured output normalization + repair pipeline
P1Y-I4 Provider capability matrix + conformance suite
P1X-I9 `TextToStructuredEvaluation` blueprint over orchestrator
acceptance_criteria: The text evaluation blueprint is regression-covered across the relevant provider profiles.
The final package-owned result shape remains stable across supported providers.
Provider-specific malformed-output paths are normalized into package semantics before reaching the public result DTO.
Fallback behavior is covered where provider-profile ordering is relevant.
The tests are deterministic and network-free.
tests: Integration-style blueprint tests using package or SDK fakes only
Stable result-shape assertions across provider variants
Negative-path tests for provider-profile mismatch or structured-output failure
risks: Risk of overly shallow fakes that do not reflect real package semantics
Risk of accidental result-shape drift while hardening parity behavior
Risk of treating one provider’s happy path as the reference instead of package semantics
docs: Use this workflow as a documented parity reference once the tests and behavior are stable

issues.title: P1Y-I6 Tests: mixed-provider `AudioToTextToEvaluation` stage parity
issues.summary: Add deterministic mixed-provider stage parity coverage for `AudioToTextToEvaluation` so the package can prove that staged transcription-plus-evaluation workflows preserve package behavior even when different provider profiles satisfy different stages.
issues.rationale:
Audio-to-text-to-evaluation is a high-value migration workflow because it combines staged provider capabilities rather than relying on a single simple request/response path. This is exactly the kind of place where users will notice lost functionality if the package cannot preserve the practical behavior they relied on.

This issue proves that staged agent-kit workflows can replace assistant-era expectations without forcing one-provider execution.
scope: Exercise transcription and evaluation stages with different compatible provider profiles
Assert stable package-owned final result DTO shape across mixed-provider stage combinations
Assert stage-local capability mismatch behavior and typed failures
Assert provider-profile routing and trace lineage across staged execution
Keep tests deterministic and network-free
out_of_scope: Live provider execution
Adding media pipelines beyond the shipped flagship audio workflow
Changing the public result contract for provider-specific stage variants
dependencies: P1Y-I4 Provider capability matrix + conformance suite
P1Y-I5 Tests: cross-provider `TextToStructuredEvaluation` parity
P1X-I11 `AudioToTextToEvaluation` blueprint over orchestrator
acceptance_criteria: The staged audio blueprint is regression-covered across mixed-provider stage combinations that satisfy the package capability matrix.
The final package-owned result shape remains stable regardless of provider mix.
Stage capability mismatches fail explicitly with package-owned failures.
Execution traces preserve correct provider-profile lineage across stage boundaries.
The tests are deterministic and network-free.
tests: Integration-style staged blueprint tests using deterministic fakes
Mixed-provider routing assertions
Negative-path tests for missing transcription or structured-output capability
risks: Risk of mixed-stage assumptions drifting away from package provider-policy rules
Risk of overfitting tests to one staged combination and missing other real migration paths
Risk of trace regressions if provider-profile lineage is not asserted tightly
docs: Document staged provider requirements once parity coverage is proven

issues.title: P1Y-I7 Normalize provider failures, refusals, and telemetry into package semantics
issues.summary: Normalize provider failures, refusal behavior, and execution telemetry into stable package semantics so users switching from `laravel-ai-assistant` do not lose clarity, observability, or predictable failure handling when package workflows cross provider boundaries.
issues.rationale:
Functional replacement is not only about successful outputs. Users also depend on understandable failure modes, refusal behavior, and consistent signals when things go wrong. If provider-specific failure payloads or incomplete telemetry leak upward, switching users will experience that as a regression even when success-path behavior is strong.

This issue makes failure and telemetry behavior part of the capability-preservation story.
scope: Map provider/runtime failures into package-owned failure categories
Normalize refusal-style outcomes into package semantics where applicable
Preserve redacted-by-default telemetry and trace metadata
Ensure failover and provider-profile transitions remain visible through package telemetry without leaking raw provider event payloads
Keep failure semantics reusable across orchestration, blueprints, and any later migration-facing surfaces
out_of_scope: Exposing raw provider failure payloads as the stable package contract
Logging raw prompt or user content by default
Provider-specific public exception types
dependencies: P0-I10 Normalize/enrich SDK events into package telemetry
P1-I3 Failover policy + typed exceptions
P1Y-I3 Structured output normalization + repair pipeline
acceptance_criteria: Provider failures, refusals, and failover exhaustion are represented through package-owned semantics.
Telemetry remains redacted by default and package-owned.
Failover and provider-profile transitions are observable without raw provider payload leakage.
The normalized failure model is reusable across the relevant package execution paths.
Deterministic tests cover the main failure categories.
tests: Unit tests for failure-category mapping and normalization
Integration tests for failover and refusal behavior using deterministic fakes
Telemetry redaction assertions for normalized runtime and orchestration events
risks: Risk of over-normalizing and losing actionable distinction between failures
Risk of raw provider payload leakage through exception context or telemetry
Risk of inconsistency between blueprint, runtime, and orchestration failure semantics
docs: Update failure and telemetry docs once the normalized package behavior is stable

issues.title: P1Y-I8 Ship Gemini/xAI and mixed-provider profile presets + examples
issues.summary: Ship tested provider-profile presets and realistic examples for Gemini, xAI, and mixed-provider workflows that reflect the actual assistant-class use cases users may want to preserve when switching to agent-kit.
issues.rationale:
Examples and presets should reinforce real capability preservation, not just provider branding. Once the audited capability gaps are understood and the package behavior is hardened, users need concrete, tested starting points that show how to express those workflows in package terms.

This issue turns the parity work into usable package configuration and examples.
scope: Ship example provider-profile presets for the relevant supported providers and staged combinations
Provide examples that cover real assistant-class workflows expressed through package blueprints or orchestrator-backed execution
Ensure examples align with the provider capability matrix and parity tests
Avoid suggesting one-to-one legacy API emulation as the recommended migration path
Keep all examples package-owned and architecture-aligned
out_of_scope: Provider marketing comparisons without tested package behavior
Examples that bypass orchestrator, blueprints, provider policy, or package memory semantics
Undocumented experimental provider surfaces
dependencies: P1Y-I4 Provider capability matrix + conformance suite
P1Y-I5 Tests: cross-provider `TextToStructuredEvaluation` parity
P1Y-I6 Tests: mixed-provider `AudioToTextToEvaluation` stage parity
acceptance_criteria: Profile presets and examples exist for the relevant supported providers and mixed-provider workflows.
Examples are grounded in tested package behavior rather than aspirational parity claims.
Examples reinforce package-owned workflow usage rather than raw provider emulation.
Config and example snippets remain compatible with the current package architecture and validation rules.
Examples are usable by switching users without implying one-to-one API cloning.
tests: Config validation tests for preset examples where practical
Snippet verification and documentation review
Regression checks that examples do not contradict tested package behavior
risks: Risk of examples drifting from real package behavior if not tied to parity tests
Risk of overselling a provider workflow the package has not truly hardened
Risk of users misreading examples as a commitment to full API emulation
docs: Update README or example docs only after presets are backed by the implemented parity work

issues.title: P1Y-I9 Migration guide: `laravel-ai-assistant` -> `laravel-ai-agent-kit`
issues.summary: Produce a practical migration guide for switching users only after the audited capability gaps are closed enough that the guide can explain how to preserve real functionality rather than offer speculative API mapping.
issues.rationale:
A migration guide is useful, but it is not the first-order problem. Writing it too early would lock in assumptions before the package can genuinely preserve the capabilities users care about. Once the functionality is there, however, a guide becomes the right place to explain how assistant-era use cases map into package-owned workflows, provider profiles, memory behavior, tools, and staged blueprints.

This keeps documentation downstream of real capability coverage.
scope: Explain how assistant-era use cases map into package-owned orchestrator and blueprint flows
Document what functionality is preserved directly, what is preserved through different package primitives, and what remains intentionally out of scope
Avoid one-to-one API mapping promises unless the package genuinely ships a compatibility-oriented facade
Document provider-profile, memory, tool, and staged workflow considerations relevant to switching users
Ground all guidance in implemented and tested package behavior
out_of_scope: Writing migration guidance before the capability gaps are closed
Promising one-to-one legacy API parity without real package support
Using the migration guide as a substitute for missing implementation work
dependencies: P1Y-I1 Define assistant replacement surface + compatibility contract
P1Y-I5 Tests: cross-provider `TextToStructuredEvaluation` parity
P1Y-I6 Tests: mixed-provider `AudioToTextToEvaluation` stage parity
P1Y-I8 Ship Gemini/xAI and mixed-provider profile presets + examples
acceptance_criteria: The guide explains how switching users preserve meaningful functionality in package terms.
The guide avoids implying one-to-one API matching unless a dedicated compatibility surface truly exists.
All claims in the guide are backed by implemented and tested package behavior.
The guide clearly separates preserved functionality, changed usage patterns, and intentional non-goals.
The guide supports real switching decisions rather than speculative planning.
tests: Documentation review
Snippet verification where practical
Cross-check against the audited capability matrix and implemented parity behavior
risks: Risk of writing the guide too early and locking in unstable assumptions
Risk of presenting architecture-aligned workflows as regressions instead of valid replacements
Risk of over-promising legacy parity
docs: This issue is the migration-documentation vehicle once the capability work is real
issues.execution_note: Do not start this issue until the relevant capability-gap issues are completed. This guide should describe proven functionality, not planned functionality.

issues.title: P1Y-I10 Release gate: assistant replacement readiness checklist
issues.summary: Create a release gate that determines whether Laravel AI Agent Kit is genuinely ready to serve as a functional replacement for the meaningful capability surface that `laravel-ai-assistant` users relied on.
issues.rationale:
The package should not claim replacement readiness based on architectural intent alone. It needs a concrete checklist that ties the audited capability target, implemented parity work, deterministic tests, provider coverage, and migration-facing guidance into one release decision.

This issue prevents premature replacement claims and keeps the bar tied to real package behavior.
scope: Create a checklist tied to the audited capability matrix from P1Y-I1
Require the relevant parity, normalization, and staged-workflow issues to be complete and tested
Require provider capability claims to be backed by deterministic package tests
Require any migration-facing or example guidance to be grounded in implemented behavior
Require explicit confirmation that package-owned boundaries, security defaults, and telemetry rules remain intact
out_of_scope: Marketing launch content
Replacing real tests or implementation work with checklist-only approval
Declaring readiness based on docs alone
dependencies: P1Y-I1 Define assistant replacement surface + compatibility contract
P1Y-I3 Structured output normalization + repair pipeline
P1Y-I4 Provider capability matrix + conformance suite
P1Y-I5 Tests: cross-provider `TextToStructuredEvaluation` parity
P1Y-I6 Tests: mixed-provider `AudioToTextToEvaluation` stage parity
P1Y-I7 Normalize provider failures, refusals, and telemetry into package semantics
P1Y-I8 Ship Gemini/xAI and mixed-provider profile presets + examples
P1Y-I9 Migration guide: `laravel-ai-assistant` -> `laravel-ai-agent-kit`
acceptance_criteria: A release-readiness checklist exists and is tied to the audited capability target rather than vague replacement language.
The checklist requires implemented parity work and deterministic test evidence, not aspiration.
The checklist verifies package-owned boundaries, security defaults, and telemetry behavior remain intact.
The checklist can be used to decide whether switching users are likely to lose meaningful functionality.
The checklist is clear enough to support future release reviews without reinterpretation.
tests: Checklist/spec issue; add validation or docs tests only if the checklist is embedded in a verified package doc artifact
Cross-check the checklist against completed parity issues before marking it done
risks: Risk of creating a vague checklist that cannot block weak release claims
Risk of readiness criteria drifting away from the audited capability matrix
Risk of treating docs completion as equivalent to capability completion
docs: Reference the final checklist from the release-hardening or migration documentation once it is valid
